content.value_statement: Building MCP servers requires protocol, SDK, and evaluation choices that are easy to miss. This skill guides planning, implementation, testing, and Microsoft ecosystem decisions for reliable integrations.
actual_capabilities: Compares Microsoft-provided MCP servers with custom server scenarios.
Guides protocol review, transport selection, and SDK selection.
Describes TypeScript, Python, and C# implementation checkpoints.
Covers tool schemas, output schemas, annotations, pagination, and error handling.
Defines build, inspector, syntax, and evaluation review steps.
Lists reference sources for MCP, SDK, Microsoft, and language-specific guides.
limitations: Does not include full runnable server source code in this file.
Requires external documentation fetches for SDK details.
Does not validate the final MCP server automatically.
May need updates as SDK APIs and Microsoft offerings change.

use_cases.title: Plan a Service Integration
use_cases.description: Map an external API into MCP tools, transports, schemas, and implementation phases before writing code.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Microsoft Options
use_cases.description: Decide whether Azure, Foundry, Fabric, Playwright, or GitHub MCP servers cover the required workflow.

use_cases.title: Create Server Evaluations
use_cases.description: Design read-only evaluation questions that test whether agents can use a server for realistic tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Server
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mcp-builder-ms to plan an MCP server for [service]. Recommend tools, transport, SDK, and first implementation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose SDK and Transport
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare TypeScript, Python, and C# for an MCP server that connects to [service]. Recommend a transport and explain tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Design the Tool Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Design MCP tools for these API endpoints: [endpoints]. Include names, input constraints, output shape, annotations, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Build Evaluation Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a read-only evaluation plan for this MCP server: [tool list]. Include realistic questions, answer checks, and stability notes.

output_examples.input: Plan an MCP server for a ticketing API.
output: A recommendation to use TypeScript with streamable HTTP for a remote multi-user service.
A phased plan covering API research, tool names, schemas, pagination, errors, tests, and evaluations.
A note to check whether an existing Microsoft or GitHub MCP server already covers the workflow.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed MCP tool list for a storage service.
output: Feedback on missing read operations, unsafe write annotations, vague descriptions, and incomplete pagination.
Suggested improvements for tool names, input constraints, structured outputs, and actionable error messages.

output_examples.input: Create evaluation coverage for an MCP server.
output: A set of independent read-only evaluation scenarios with stable answers.
Guidance for verifying each answer before using the evaluation.

best_practices: Check existing Microsoft and ecosystem MCP servers before building a custom server.
Design tool names, schemas, and descriptions for agent discovery and predictable use.
Test builds, inspect tools, and create read-only evaluations before release.
anti_patterns: Do not mirror every API endpoint without considering agent workflows.
Do not omit pagination, output schemas, or actionable error messages.
Do not publish a server without testing realistic read-only evaluation tasks.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps plan and implement MCP servers for external services using TypeScript, Python, or C# patterns.

faq.question: Does it create a complete server automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, checkpoints, and prompts for building and reviewing your server.

faq.question: When should I use an existing Microsoft MCP server?
faq.answer: Use one when Azure, Foundry, Fabric, Playwright, or GitHub MCP already covers your required workflow.

faq.question: Does it cover remote and local transports?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains streamable HTTP for remote servers and stdio for local development use cases.

faq.question: Can it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is compatible with MCP-aware development in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: It covers authentication planning, read-only evaluation design, tool annotations, and error handling basics.
